reasoning: The probability of a complete draw-color sequence in a Polya urn is a product of rising per-color factors divided by the common total rising product, hence invariant under permutations of draw positions. By exchangeability and consistency under marginalization, a specified subsequence of n draw positions has the same joint law as the first n draws. Multiply the n requested color probabilities with only previously requested colors reinforced; the actual gaps x_i do not enter. Compute numerator and denominator as exact integers and reduce once by their gcd. This is not treating reinforcement as independent draws; the count of previous requested occurrences is retained.
